text:
lina-sales: Need help prepping for TelcoCorp POC. They require: EU-only data processing, control-plane residency in EU, BYOK (HSM), and a signed subproc attestation. AE asked for a short decision matrix (hosted vs dedicated vs private) + rough cost delta and lead times. Who owns what?

theo-ops: I can scope ops feasibility. Quick Q: do they need tenant-level pinning (sticky routing) or full regional isolation?

lina-sales: Tenant-level pinning should be sufficient for POC, but legal insists on no control-plane telemetry leaving EU.

rachel-legal: If control-plane must stay in EU, hosted offering won't meet that unless we provision Private control plane or a dedicated EU-only control plane. We'll need DPA + subproc export + SOC2 dates. Also request: IP allowlist and mTLS for KMS traffic.

devin-pricing: I can draft numbers. Inputs: expected QPS, avg tokens/request, POC length.

lina-sales: POC inputs: 8 qps baseline, 30 qps peaks (2 min bursts), avg 150 tokens per request, 30 day POC.

yuri-ml: Model-wise they want a 13B quantized variant. Memory profile small; should fit on a single pod with reserved throughput.

theo-ops: Ops notes: three deployment patterns:
- HOSTED+GEO_PIN: data path pinned to eu-west and inference runs in EU region. Control-plane remains multiregion (not EU-only). Fastest to stand up (~3 business days), lowest cost, limited attestation.
- DEDICATED: Reserved GPU pool in EU with tenant isolation. Control-plane still hosted unless we combine with Private control plane. Setup ~2-3 weeks.
- PRIVATE: Customer-dedicated control plane + data plane in their VPC or our EU-only control plane. Full residency compliance, longer lead time (~4-6 weeks).

ops-bot: Presales checklist snippet:
```
routing: "sticky_tenant_pin: eu-west-1"
control_plane: "eu_only: true|false"
kms: "BYOK-HSM: external endpoints, mTLS required"
network: "ip_allowlist, nat, peering, egress_routes"
```
Include note about fallback: "fallback: model_fallback_to_lower_latency_variant"

rachel-legal: For BYOK-HSM we need to know whether customer will host HSM in their cloud (customer-managed) or on-prem. Hosted HSM endpoints require mutual TLS and certificate exchange; include time for cert stamping.

anita-se: From AE/Customer side: they prefer managed but insist that keys never traverse non-EU infrastructure. That pushes towards Private. They asked whether we can provide 3rd-party attestation for subproc list and a signed DPA addendum.

devin-pricing: Ballpark monthly cost for a 30-day POC:
- HOSTED+GEO_PIN: ~$2,500 (incl. short-term egress SLA) + one-time networking $3,500
- DEDICATED (small reserved pool): ~$9,000/month (minimum 1-month commit) + onboarding $2,000
- PRIVATE (control-plane in EU): ~$18,000/month + integration SOW ~$8k, lead time +4-6 weeks
These are rough. I'll validate with finance.

theo-ops: Additional ops caveat: hosted + BYOK-HSM requires opening outbound connections to customer HSM endpoints; if customer firewall blocks that, we'll need to set up a peered path or run HSM connector in their VPC (Private). That affects timeline.

lina-sales: Great. Can someone assemble a one-pager matrix with columns: Security posture, Cost estimate, Lead time, Operational complexity, Recommended for POC? Need this by EOD so AE can send to customer.

yuri-ml: I'll add a short note recommending model quantization profile and expected latency for the 13B model under the POC load.

rachel-legal: I'll pull subprocessor list + SOC2 cert timestamps and prepare DPA addendum template. Need contact at TelcoCorp for cert acceptance.

devin-pricing: I'll put the numbers into a clean one-pager and include a footnote about BYOK integration SOW costs.

anita-se: I'll collect customer confirmation on whether they accept hosted control-plane if we provide a signed attestation that no payloads leave EU.

lina-sales: Action items summary: @devin-pricing one-pager, @theo-ops ops playbook & network checklist, @yuri-ml latency + quant notes, @rachel-legal subproc + DPA draft, @anita-se confirm customer acceptance. I'll schedule 20m sync tomorrow 10:30 CET. Thanks all :thumbsup:
